extracted.intended_audience: organizations and individuals seeking funding or information about Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation grantmaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance about who the Gates Foundation funds, how its funding works (grants vs investments), how applicants are identified/selected, and the Foundation's priorities and policies. Useful for prospective grantees, partners, and donors seeking to understand eligibility, mechanisms, and organizational principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission focus / strategic goals
rubrics_metrics.description: “Our mission is to create a world where every person has the opportunity to live a healthy, productive life.” The Foundation works to dramatically reduce disease and poverty and build a more equal world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding is directed toward global health and development priorities that align with this mission; applicants should align proposals with the Foundation’s aim to improve health, economic opportunity, and maternal/child health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority for interventions with large impact potential
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation “focuses on innovative products, ideas, and approaches that have the potential to save and improve the greatest number of lives.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate potential for large-scale impact (saving/improving many lives) and innovation relative to existing solutions. The Foundation’s efforts span more than four dozen program areas and engage many types of partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary selection mode: proactive outreach and invitation
rubrics_metrics.description: “In most cases, we directly contact organizations identified by our staff and invite them to submit funding proposals for work that addresses a specific foundation priority, such as nutrition, tuberculosis prevention, or safer childbirth.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most grants are made by invitation after Foundation staff identify organizations; unsolicited proposals are typically not the primary route. Applicants should expect outreach rather than open application unless otherwise posted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occasional open solicitations / posted requests for proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: “We also award some grants through posted requests for proposals, including through our Grand Challenges initiatives.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor published RFPs and Grand Challenges calls for opportunities; these are the primary public entry points for organizations not contacted directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of funding mechanisms (grants and investments)
rubrics_metrics.description: “We make grants to organizations as well as investments in projects carried out by private companies.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation uses both traditional grants to nonprofits and investment vehicles for private-sector projects. Applicants should understand which mechanism matches their entity type and the project’s financing needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for experience and expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: “We pursue our goals by providing funding to those who have the experience and expertise to make an impact.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate relevant track record, capacity, and technical or operational expertise to implement and scale the proposed work; proposals lacking demonstrated capability are less likely to be funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on partnership and convening role
rubrics_metrics.description: “We fund and bring together people and organizations in the global health and development sectors so we can collectively accelerate progress on urgent issues.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation values partnerships and collaborative approaches; proposals that describe effective collaboration, alignment with other actors, and a convening or catalytic role may be favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of finances and policies
rubrics_metrics.description: “We are committed to providing clear, timely information on our finances and grantmaking efforts. See information about our annual reports, audited financial statements, charitable work with the private sector, and the Foundation Trust.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Foundation publishes financials, policies, and a searchable database of committed grants (payments made and committed from 1994 onward). Prospective grantees can consult these resources to understand past funding and Foundation practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: No direct donations accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: “Does the Gates Foundation accept direct donations? No. We encourage people who support our goals to give directly to our grantees… or donate to Gates Philanthropy Partners, a 501(c)(3) public charity that aligns its grantmaking with the foundation’s strategic goals.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals and organizations should not attempt to donate directly to the Foundation; instead give to listed grantees or the Foundation’s public charity partner if they wish to support aligned work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fraud and scam awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: “I got an email saying I won a foundation lottery or a prize from Bill Gates. Is this true? No, this is a scam. … We encourage you to report such fraudulent communications.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious of unsolicited prize/lottery notifications or communications purporting to be from the Foundation; verify authenticity and report suspected fraud to the Foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Gates Foundation was founded on a simple premise: that people everywhere, regardless of identity or circumstances, should have the chance to live healthy, productive lives.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DEI principles guide the Foundation’s work; applicants should consider and address equity implications of proposed work and alignment with the Foundation’s DEI commitments.
